newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBS FIRMER, BOOSTED BY RISE IN U.S. TREASURIES.
newsitem.headline: JGBS FIRMER, BOOSTED BY RISE IN U.S. TREASURIES.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract was slightly higher in early morning trade on Thursday due to a rise in U.S. Treasury bonds overnight, traders said.
"Overnight U.S. economic data defused fears of a possible rise in U.S. interest rates, and boosted U.S. Treasury bonds and this has lent support to JGBs," a trust bank trader said.
The September's rise toward the end of Tokyo trade on Wednesday was also considered a postive factor, traders said.
This may mean that long liquidation has abated for now, a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
The September stood at 126.59 as of 0043 GMT, up from Wednesday's close of 126.48.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.110 percent, down from the previous day's close of 2.125 percent.
There was little impact from an International Monetary Fund (IMF) report saying it would likely be desirable for Japan to begin raising interest rates later in the year, traders said.

"The IMF said it would be desirable for Japan to raise rates if the negative effects from a rise in the consumption tax recede. But market players do not think that such a scenario is very likely," the first trader said.
